Practice what the module taught you.

Take a written exam on database concepts, write queries against five practice tables, or build your own tables and relationships. Study the five midterm modules, with notes on MariaDB differences and clearly marked additional practice.

Original module · 105 pages

SQL practice runs in your browser and follows MariaDB 10.4 syntax. See the module notes for SQL differences and available commands.
Module notes and available commands
  • p.56: FULL JOIN is shown as valid SQL, but MariaDB/MySQL has no native full-join keyword. FULL can be read as a table alias; FULL OUTER JOIN is invalid syntax. The LEFT/RIGHT JOIN with UNION workaround is beyond the module and removes duplicate result rows.
  • p.72: the prose says the second column sorts descending, but its example contains no DESC. Keep the printed SQL and interpret its actual default ascending order.
  • p.39: the DATETIME minimum of 1753 comes from SQL Server. MariaDB/MySQL DATETIME uses a 1000 minimum. The earlier audit referred to p.32/39; p.32 itself discusses numeric types.
  • p.33–34: REAL is described as single precision. Under this XAMPP SQL mode, REAL is a synonym for DOUBLE; REAL_AS_FLOAT changes that behavior.
  • p.38–39: the module includes general SQL temporal wording. MariaDB DATE starts at 1000; TIME can represent durations beyond 24 hours; TIME WITHOUT TIME ZONE is not MariaDB syntax. TIMESTAMP converts between the session time zone and UTC rather than retaining a zone name.
  • p.58–59: a semicolon ends an interactive monitor statement. Run and Check require complete terminators; an unfinished batch executes nothing. The monitor alternative \G displays results vertically. The printed Access CREATE TABLE example also omits a comma after PropositionID INTEGER.
  • p.62: COMMENT ON TABLE is another SQL dialect’s syntax. MariaDB uses a COMMENT table option, which is additional syntax beyond the module examples.
  • p.84: the short-circuit result is correct. Division-by-zero diagnostics depend on statement type and SQL mode; do not treat the prose as a universal error rule.
  • Supported: the module’s demonstrated CREATE/DROP DATABASE and TABLE, ALTER, RENAME, TRUNCATE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT clauses and joins, SHOW, USE, DESCRIBE, COMMIT, SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK, GRANT and REVOKE forms; its taught data types and primary/unique/not-null constraints.
  • Additional commands beyond module examples: START TRANSACTION, BEGIN, ROLLBACK TO, RELEASE SAVEPOINT, SET AUTOCOMMIT, IF EXISTS, IF NOT EXISTS, SHOW WARNINGS/GRANTS, explicit foreign-key constraints (including connections using several columns or referring to the same table) and MariaDB table COMMENT options. Omit ON DELETE/ON UPDATE clauses for the supported default RESTRICT behavior; CASCADE/SET NULL extensions are outside this lab. In MariaDB 10.4, inline column REFERENCES shorthand is accepted but creates no enforced foreign key. COALESCE/IFNULL are in the module; other scalar functions in the lab are supporting features.
  • All browser queries use the offline root account. GRANT/REVOKE targets are simulated locally and can be inspected using SHOW GRANTS; no login or account switching is involved. Generated timestamps use the browser’s local clock, with millisecond precision. Server timezone changes and server storage statistics are outside the offline model. SQL mode mirrors XAMPP’s non-strict configuration, so some bad values produce warnings and coerced values. This is a study engine, not the full MariaDB server: subqueries, views, stored programs, window functions, arbitrary server variables and other extensions are identified as practice limitations.
  • p.45: “SHOW TABLE standing” is a transcription error; the monitor command is SHOW TABLE STATUS LIKE 'tablename' \G. Offline status output omits physical server statistics.
  • p.101: the RIGHT JOIN prose names the wrong side for NULL padding. Unmatched right rows have NULL in the left-table columns, as the p.100 and p.103 examples demonstrate.
  • p.41: invalid ENUM inputs can warn and coerce to the empty error value under this non-strict XAMPP mode; the module’s unconditional error wording does not apply to every SQL mode.
